title: The One in the Drawer
subtitle: 科技与创新 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科技与创新（科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）
meta: 主题语境：科技与创新（科学与技术·科技发展与信息技术创新、科学精神）　|　核心词汇：battery　|　正文 347 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 battery 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my father bought ① a battery for a radio and carried it home like a child, and my mother said the carrying was the whole of the purchase. The ② battery, meaning the thing in the box and not the radio, lasted eleven months and was never replaced; a battery, he said, is the only object that is bought for what it will stop doing.

Every ③ battery in that house was kept in the cold, and the ④ battery in the drawer, meaning the one saved for the winter and not either of those, was found dead in March and kept for another year. A battery, my grandmother said, is nine parts habit and one part a date you have forgotten; my father said the habit is the part that costs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ battery was the whole of the guns, meaning the line of them and not the cells. The ⑥ battery, meaning the row and not any of that, is the only thing on a hill that is counted and never used; a battery, he said, is either something you put in a radio or the only word that means both a cell and a line of guns. She said the line came first.

By 1974 the ⑦ battery had become a word in an argument about the car, and the car had become an argument about who had left the lights on. The ⑧ battery of the whole thing, my father wrote in June, was eleven months of sound and one dead cell; a battery, he said, is either the thing in the box or the reason you learned to check. She said the checking was the part nobody did.

The ⑨ battery I remember is the one in the drawer, which was dead in 1976 and was still in the drawer in 1979. A ⑩ battery, my mother said in 1981, is the only object that improves by being forgotten; every battery, she said, is a habit that has agreed to look like a cell. He said the habit was the expensive part.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 电池（指盒子里那个东西，与收音机相对）
C. 固定搭配：buy a battery 买一节电池
D. n. 电池（指屋里每一节）
E. n. 电池（指抽屉里那一节）
F. n. 炮组；排炮（指那一排炮）
G. n. 炮组（抽象：那一排／一组）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The battery, meaning the thing in the box and not the radio
battery was the whole of the guns
the battery had become a word in an argument about the car
The battery of the whole thing
A battery, my mother said in 1981

answers.why: buy a battery 意为“买一节电池”，1959 年父亲给收音机买了一节电池，像抱孩子一样抱回家。
battery 意为“电池”，指盒子里那个东西而不是收音机，它撑了十一个月，从此再没换过。
battery 指屋里每一节电池，那屋里每一节都存放在阴凉处。
battery 指抽屉里那一节（留着过冬的那一节），三月发现已经没电，却又放了一年。
battery 意为“炮组、排炮”，指那一排炮，叔叔说 battery 就是那些炮的全部。
battery 为抽象用法，指那一排／一组，是山上唯一被清点却从没用过的东西。
battery 意为“电池”，到 1974 年这个 battery 成了一场关于汽车的争吵里的一个词。
battery 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，父亲六月写道，整件事权衡下来是十一个月的声音和一节没电的电池。
battery 意为“电池”，我记得的是抽屉里那一节，1976 年就没电了，1979 年还在抽屉里。
battery 为抽象总称，母亲说电池是唯一会因为被遗忘而变好的物件。
